body.x: Apollon (CEO Hong Aram) participated in CES 2025 Unveiled, a global media event held on January 5th (local time) before the official opening of CES 2025.

Apollon develops needle-free continuous glucose monitors (CGMs) and holds proprietary technology for ultra-compact devices that use Raman spectroscopy signals to detect glucose in the body. Since its establishment in 2021, Apollon has filed and registered over 30 patents related to this field in South Korea and the United States.

Apollon has earned recognition for its technological innovation, winning awards such as the Minister of SMEs and Startups Award, TIPS Program Selection, LG Open Innovation Grand Prize, and the CES Innovation Award. In 2023, the company established a U.S. subsidiary in Cambridge, Massachusetts, to solidify its plans to enter the U.S. market, representing the largest CGM sector globally.

Apollon unveiled its noninvasive and ultracompact CGM, MOGLU, at CES 2025 Unveiled. This next-generation CGM combines advanced engineering with user-centric design. It eliminates the need for needles and sensor replacements and offers exceptional efficiency compared to traditional glucose monitors.

MOGLU employs Raman spectroscopy to focus on specific glucose signals, bypassing the conventional full-spectrum analysis approach. This eliminates the need for gratings, drastically reducing the device's size and enhancing user convenience.

The device also uses narrow-band filters placed in front of high-sensitivity photodiodes to transmit specific Raman signals selectively. This optimization of the optical path improves the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and maximizes energy efficiency.

body.cap: | Overseas media representatives visiting Apollon's booth at CES 2025 Unveiled. | Photo by Aving News

body.x: Unlike spectrometers using CMOS sensors, MOGLU employs multiple photodiodes to reduce dark noise at room temperature significantly. It eliminates unnecessary wavelengths and captures only desired signals for superior SNR performance.

In addition, MOGLU uses an 830nm laser to measure glucose levels in the body directly, meeting FDA standards. This approach demonstrates superior accuracy and safety compared to indirect measurement methods. The device causes no skin irritation, is smaller than a smartwatch, and features a form factor similar to existing CGMs, allowing users to transition seamlessly.

An Apollon representative highlighted, "MOGLU is designed to be worn on the wrist, arm, or other body parts, offering high usability. It does not require sensor replacements, significantly reducing waste and maintenance inconveniences. Moreover, its low power consumption ensures stable daily performance and real-time data is transmitted to a mobile app, enabling effective glucose management without disrupting daily life."

The representative added, "Apollon plans to expand beyond the domestic market into the U.S. with innovative products like MOGLU. To this end, we will actively engage with domestic and international investors during CES. We are thrilled to have received significant attention from global media at the event, especially as a CES Innovation Award winner in digital health alongside leading brands like Abbott and Dexcom."
